messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Telugu, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Telugu line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
ఆమెకు అంత చెడైన దుష్ట స్వభావం ఉంది, ఆమె ఎప్పుడూ తన లొభించే కోరికను తీరించదు, ఆమె భోజనానికి తర్వాత ముందు కన్నా ఎక్కువ ఆకలిగా ఉంటుంది.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (Telugu → English) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------| | e (97) | clause‑linking conjunction | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (omitted) | | ha (97) | verb “has” (possession) | ఉంది | “exists / has” | **OK** | | natura | noun “nature” (inherent quality) | స్వభావం | “nature” | **OK** | | sì | degree adverb “so” (intensifier) | అంత | “so / that much” | **OK** | | malvagia | adjective “malign” | చెడైన | “malicious / evil” | **OK** | | e (second) | coordinating conjunction “and” (joins adjectives) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | ria | adjective “evil” | దుష్ట | “wicked / evil” | **OK** | | che (98) | relative pronoun “that” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | mai | adverb “never” | ఎప్పుడూ | “ever / never” | **OK** | | non | negative particle “not” (part of double‑negative) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (negation expressed in verb) | | empie | verb “fills / satisfies” | — | — | **MISSING** (positive verb not rendered) | | la | definite article “the” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | bramosa | adjective “greedy” | లొభించే | “greedy / covetous” | **OK** | | voglia | noun “will / desire” | కోరికను | “desire (accusative)” | **OK** | | e (99) | coordinating conjunction “and” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | dopo | preposition “after” | తర్వాత | “after” | **OK** | | ’l (elided *il*) | definite article “the” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | pasto | noun “meal” | భోజనానికి | “to the meal” (dative) | **OK** | | ha (99) | verb “has” (state) | ఉంటుంది | “is / exists” | **OK** | | più | comparative adverb “more” | అధిక | “more / greater” | **OK** | | fame | noun “hunger” | ఆకలిగా | “hungry (adverbial) / hunger” | **OK** | | che (comparative) | comparative conjunction “than” | కన్నా | “than” | **OK** | | pria | adverb “before” | ముందు | “before” | **OK** |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: e (97), e (second), che (98), non, la, e (99), ’l, e (97) – these function words are naturally omitted in Telugu. - **MISSING**: empie – the positive verb “fills / satisfies” is not explicitly present; its meaning is conveyed together with the negation in the verb “తీరించదు”. - No **WRONG**, **GRAMMAR**, or **UNNECESSARY** lexical items beyond the expected omissions.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Telugu script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
